subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Quantal Response Equilibrium
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Quantal Response Equilibrium.

hook.text: A player picks the better option 70% of the time, not 100%. They know which is better but occasionally choose the worse.

buildup.text: Quantal Response Equilibrium sets up the incentives, biases, and tradeoffs driving the choice.

discovery.text: McKelvey and Palfrey showed QRE explains data better than Nash in many games.

twist.text: As stakes increase, behavior gets closer to Nash. Higher payoffs motivate more careful thinking.

climax.text: QRE teaches a practical lesson: expect opponents to make mistakes, and plan for error, both theirs and yours.

punchline.text: We choose well most of the time. But not all of the time.

quiz.question: What does QRE suggest about decision-making?
options: People always choose the mathematically optimal option
Better options are chosen more often but noise causes occasional errors
People choose randomly regardless of payoffs
